messages:
sam support: Hey team — AcmeCorp opened a billing dispute. They say a lot of streaming calls that ended with client disconnects (mobile app backgrounding) are being billed and show up as 5xx in their dashboard. They provided some request_ids. Can we triage?

maria-cs: Customer sent logs + timeline. They see short-lived streams (100-500ms) where client cancels, but our UI shows these as `5xx` and tokens billed. They included this convo id: req=acme-req-2026-03-14-77

jess-eng-runtime: Thanks — can you paste one of the raw request ids and a minimal repro? Any curl or SDK snippet helps. Also, did they use chunked encoding or websockets?

maria-cs: They use our streaming REST endpoint (chunked encoding). Example curl they sent:

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDFOO" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-2-large","input":"hello","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Client cancels by closing the TCP connection after ~200ms. They claim tokens are still counted and calls classified 5xx in dashboard.

rod-sre: I pulled logs for req=acme-req-2026-03-14-77 and nearby reqs. Gateway shows: `upstream write failed: broken pipe` and our router emitted `status=502` for the request. Attached snippet: `router[conn=xyz]: writev failed: ECONNRESET by peer`

rod-sre: Important: the backend inference node actually returned partial output before the client closed. We forwarded bytes, then the client FINed, which produced an EPIPE on the gateway when writing the last chunk. That path currently maps to 5xx counts.

jess-eng-runtime: Hmm. Historically we considered write errors to client as 5xx only if the backend errored. If backend produced bytes and finished normally but the client dropped, the richer classification should be client-abort (4xx-ish) and excluded from billing. I need the exact log lines + request IDs to correlate with billing events.

sam support: Provided three request_ids: acme-req-2026-03-14-77, acme-req-2026-03-14-82, acme-req-2026-03-14-95. Customer says ~30% of their streaming sessions are mobile app cancels so this is a material amount.

jess-eng-runtime: I grepped the router code. There's a recent change (commit efd1234) that changed classification in streaming path: `classify_stream_abort()` now treats any EPIPE/EINTR during response write as `5xx` for metrics. That looks suspicious. I opened a quick diff: previously we checked `backend_status` and only marked server_error if backend returned >=500 or connection closed unexpectedly. The new code conflates client write errors with backend failure.

rod-sre: Repro steps I used locally: start a small server that sends a chunk and sleeps, then close the client. Command: `python -m http.server` won't stream nicely, but here's a minimal Node snippet I used to simulate server -> client partial then client close. Also `curl --no-buffer` to stream and then Ctrl-C to emulate cancel. When client cancels we see `EPIPE` in router and it increments `router.responses.5xx.stream` metric.

jess-eng-runtime: Actionables: 1) Roll back commit efd1234 on the router classification toggle for streaming (safe, hotfix). 2) Add better detection: if backend produced HEADERS/at least one chunk and backend process exited with 0, treat as client-abort and map to `4xx.client_aborted_stream` metric and exclude from billing export. 3) Add test for chunked response + client FIN that asserts billing_export omits aborted sessions.

rod-sre: Agreed. I'll flip the feature flag for the classification toggle in prod behind a canary and watch `router.responses.5xx.stream` and billing_export counts. Will note timeline for rollback at 15m intervals.

maria-cs: Customer wants ETA and reimbursement if we confirm misbilling. We'll need a list of affected request_ids and token counts for a refund.

jess-eng-runtime: Once rollback is live, I'll run a query on our metering pipeline to find sessions where `backend_status` was 200/zero-exit AND router saw write error due to EPIPE/EINTR. We'll produce a CSV: request_id, customer_id, tokens_billed, timestamp. That can be used for refunds.

ops-bot: deploy-notification: rollback of router classification flag scheduled at 2026-03-14T18:12:00Z, initiated by rod-sre, change-id: toggle-rollback-20260314-1

rod-sre: Rollback is in canary now (10% of traffic). Early signal: `router.responses.5xx.stream` dropped 78% for canary nodes. Billing export pipeline showing corresponding drop in candidate refunds.

sam support: Thanks — I'll notify AcmeCorp: we're rolling a fix and will follow up with affected request list + refund plan. Please keep me posted.

jess-eng-runtime: I'll open a PR to adjust classification and add unit + integration test against the streaming harness. Also add a note in CHANGELOG about handling client-initiated connection closes so we don't regress again.

maria-cs: Customer replied: appreciated, asking for estimated refund window. I'll give tentative 48 hours after we finish accounting query.

rod-sre: Will monitor for 30m and then promote rollback to 100% if stable. If anyone needs the raw logs I can paste them here.

sam support: 👍 please @rod-sre when promoted to 100% and send the CSV when ready.

jess-eng-runtime: copy — PR ready to review, will link once tests run.
